15Payment methodCard, or the account's direct-bill terms. Many operators require this before a booking can be saved.
Three of these are required to save a reservation

A billing contact, a pickup date and a pickup time. Everything else can technically follow later — which is exactly why agents leave gaps. "Technically saveable" and "safe to run" are different standards, and you are responsible for the second one.

Fields that quietly depend on each other

Service type → rate

Change the service type and the price changes, because a different rate table applies. Never adjust one without re-checking the other.

Flight → pickup time

On an arrival, the flight is the pickup time. A time typed by hand that does not match the flight will not move when the flight does.

Luggage → vehicle → price

A luggage answer that changes the vehicle changes the quote. Ask about bags before you quote, not after.

Lesson 2 of 3

7.2 Verifying and reading back

In plain words — Verification is the last thirty seconds of the call, and it catches more errors than everything before it. You are not re-reading the booking to the customer; you are giving them a chance to hear one thing that is wrong.

What to read back, and how

1Date, with the weekday"Thursday the 14th of September." The weekday is the error-catcher — people know what day they are flying even when they mistype the date.
2Time, with am or pm said aloud"Six o'clock in the morning." Never "0600" to a customer, and never just "six".
3Pickup address, including the specific part"1400 Market Street, the main lobby entrance."
4Destination, or the duration if hourly"To Dulles" — or "four hours as directed, starting from the hotel".
5Vehicle class and passenger name"An SUV, for Mr Okafor." Spell the surname back if it is going on a name board.
6The flight, on any airport job"United 1247, landing 2:35pm." Read the number digit by digit.
7The confirmation number, and what they will receive"That's 15449, and the confirmation's on its way to you now."

Verifying contact information

Contact details are the ones customers assume you already have, and the ones most likely to be out of date on a returning account.

Read numbers back in groups

"That's 214, 555, 0117." Reading a ten-digit number as one string is how transposed digits survive.

Confirm the email by spelling the unusual part

"d-a-n-a dot w at vertex dot com." Confirmations that bounce are discovered by the customer, not by you.

On a returning account, confirm rather than assume

"I have a mobile ending 0117 — is that still the best number for the passenger?"

Ask who to call on the day

Passenger or arranger? Corporate accounts often have a standing rule, and it belongs in the account notes.

If the caller corrects you, change it and read it back again

A correction means the call has one known error in it. It may have two. Re-reading the corrected line costs five seconds and is the cheapest insurance on the call.

Lesson 3 of 3

7.3 Knowledge check

Knowledge check

Reservation fundamentals

Pass mark: 3 of 4.

Which missing field most often causes a ride to fail at the kerb, even when everything else is correct?

Without a mobile, a driver who cannot see the passenger has no way to reach them. Almost every "the driver never showed" complaint is actually two people fifty metres apart with no phone number between them.

A booking is saved with a billing contact, a pickup date and a pickup time and nothing else. Is that acceptable?

The system's minimum and an operable reservation are different standards. If you save a partial booking, the gap belongs to you until it is filled.

On an airport arrival, what should the pickup time be based on?

A hand-typed time is static. A pickup tied to the flight tracks delays automatically, which is the entire point of collecting the flight number.

Why should a date be read back as "Thursday the 14th" rather than "the 14th"?

The weekday is the cross-check. "Thursday the 14th" against a customer who is flying Friday produces an instant correction; a bare number does not.
Phase 3 · Reservation & product knowledge

Airport transportation

≡ Syllabus · Phase 3 · Module 8
≈ 25 min
≡Definition

An airport job is any trip whose timing is decided by an aircraft rather than by the customer. That single difference is what makes it the most error-prone work an agent does, and the work customers judge most harshly.

Two reservations that look almost identical — one to the airport, one from it — behave completely differently.

»Example

A flight lands 90 minutes late. On a correctly built arrival the pickup moves with it and nobody needs to do anything. On one where an agent typed a fixed time, the driver arrives on time, waits, racks up wait time, and may leave before the passenger clears customs.

✓Key points
  • Arrival and departure are different service types, not a direction of travel
  • The flight number is what makes a trip track a delay — always take it
  • International arrivals need far more clearance time than domestic
  • Meet & greet costs money and must be asked for, not assumed
8.1 Codes, terminals and…8.2 Arrival or departure8.3 Flight monitoring, de…8.4 Meet & greet or curbs…8.5 Knowledge check
Lesson 1 of 5

8.1 Codes, terminals and the shape of an airport job

Airport codes

Airports are identified by a three-letter IATA code. You will use them constantly — in service types, in fixed-rate zones, and in conversation with dispatchers. You do not need to memorise the world; you need the ones your client serves, and the habit of confirming rather than guessing.

CodeAirportWatch for
JFK / LGA / EWRNew York areaThree airports, wildly different drive times. "New York" is not an answer.
IAD / DCA / BWIWashington areaSame problem. DCA and IAD are an hour apart in traffic.
ORD / MDWChicagoMidway is not O'Hare and the rates differ.
DFW / DALDallasLove Field is a separate zone.
LAX / BUR / LGB / SNALos Angeles areaFour options; ask which one the flight actually uses.
LHR / LGW / LCY / STNLondonCity is central; Stansted is not remotely.
Never infer the airport from the city

"Flying into New York on United 1247" does not tell you the airport. Look the flight up, or ask. A car at the wrong airport is an unrecoverable failure — the drive between JFK and EWR is longer than most transfers.

Terminals, doors and the FBO

Terminal

Which building. Often determined by the airline, but not always — codeshares land where the operating carrier sits, not the one on the ticket.

Door or pickup zone

Large airports have designated limousine zones, often on an upper level or in a garage. Many clients have a standing rule; it belongs in the account or trip notes.

FBO

A private-jet terminal — a fixed-base operator. A different address entirely, usually on the other side of the field, with its own name (Signature, Atlantic, Million Air). Always ask which FBO.

Private aviation has no flight tracking you can rely on

A private flight has a tail number, not a commercial flight number, and it will not appear in normal flight tracking. On FBO work you need a contact who will tell you when they are wheels-down — usually the arranger or the FBO itself — and the pickup is managed by hand.

Lesson 2 of 5

8.2 Arrival or departure: two different reservations

In plain words — A departure is a normal pickup that happens to end at an airport. An arrival is a completely different animal: the customer does not control the time, the pickup point is inside somebody else's building, and the clock starts when the wheels touch down.
To airport (departure)From airport (arrival)
Who sets the timeThe customer. They choose when to be collected.The aircraft. The pickup follows the flight.
Pickup locationA street address.A terminal, and within it a meeting point or a kerbside zone.
Flight numberStill take it — a cancelled outbound flight is a cancelled ride.Essential. Without it nothing tracks.
Wait time clockStarts at the scheduled pickup time.Starts at actual landing plus the grace period.
What goes wrongTraffic, and customers underestimating how early they need to leave.Delays, diversions, baggage, immigration, and passengers who do not turn their phone on.

Building a departure

1Take the flight time and the airportEven though the customer sets the pickup, you need these to sanity-check the pickup they ask for.
2Check the pickup allows enough timeIf a customer asks for a pickup that gets them to a busy international terminal 50 minutes before departure, say so. "That's tighter than we'd normally recommend — would you like me to make it 45 minutes earlier?" You advise; they decide; you record the answer.
3Confirm the terminalDeparture terminal, by airline. It goes to the driver.

Building an arrival

1Airline and flight number, read back digit by digitThis is the field the whole reservation hangs on.
2Confirm the airport and terminal from the flight, not the callerCallers say "New York". The flight says EWR.
3Set the pickup to follow the flightSet Driver Should Arrive to When your flight arrives rather than typing a clock time. A typed time will not move when the flight does.
4Set Driver Should ArriveThis is the field that adds the clearance allowance. Its options are Do not adjust based on flight arrival, When your flight arrives, and 15 / 30 / 45 / 60 / 90 / 120 min after gate arrival. Domestic arrivals with checked bags usually need 30–45; international needs 60–90 or more at peak. Use the client’s numbers.
5Decide the meeting arrangementMeet & greet inside, or kerbside with a phone call. See the next lesson.
6Take the passenger's mobile, and check it works abroadOn an international arrival, ask whether the number will be reachable on landing. A passenger with no roaming is a passenger the driver cannot call.
Domestic and international are not the same trip

The same flight number can be either, and immigration is the difference. An hour of clearance time built into a domestic arrival wastes the driver's morning; forty minutes on an international arrival leaves your passenger standing at the kerb watching the car drive away.

Lesson 3 of 5

8.3 Flight monitoring, delays and changes

Flight monitoring is the reason an operator can promise "we track your flight". What it means in practice is that a system watches the flight status and moves the spot time, and that somebody watches the exceptions the system cannot handle.

What monitoring does on its own

Delay

Landing time moves later; the spot time moves with it. Usually handled with no human involvement.

Early arrival

Flights land early more often than people expect. The spot time moves earlier — and a driver not watching may be late for an on-time flight.

Gate and terminal change

Picked up on most commercial flights. The driver needs telling; do not assume they saw it.

What monitoring cannot handle — the exceptions you work

ExceptionWhat it meansWhat you do
DivertedThe aircraft landed somewhere else entirely.Contact the arranger immediately. The existing trip is dead; a new one from the diversion airport may be needed, possibly through an affiliate. Escalate.
CancelledThe flight is not operating.Reach the passenger or arranger, establish the rebooking, and rebuild or cancel the trip. Do not cancel unilaterally — they may be on the next flight.
Long delay past the driver's next jobThe car is now double-booked.Tell dispatch. This is an operational decision, not a booking one.
Landed, passenger not appearingImmigration, baggage, or a missed connection nobody told you about.Driver waits per the grace period while you try the passenger's mobile and the arranger. Escalate before anyone leaves.
Private / FBO flightNo usable tracking.Managed by hand with a contact who will tell you when they land.
Flight number changed by the airlineThe booking is now tracking a flight the passenger is not on.Update the reservation with the new number, or monitoring is silently watching the wrong aircraft.
The dangerous case is the quiet one

A three-hour delay is loud — everyone knows. The one that catches agents out is a flight that lands early while the driver is still an hour away, or a passenger who rebooked onto a different flight and told the airline but not you. Both are silent until a passenger is standing alone at an airport.

When a flight changes: the order of work

1Confirm the change from the flight data, not from a rumourBefore acting, verify the new status.
2Update the reservationNew flight number or new time, so the record and the monitoring are correct.
3Tell dispatch and the driverThe system may not push the change to a driver who already accepted the job. Say it out loud.
4Tell the arranger"Their flight is delayed to 16:20 and we've moved the pickup." Customers are reassured by being told something they already know.
5Document all of itTime, source, what you changed, who you told.
Lesson 4 of 5

8.4 Meet & greet or curbside

In plain words — There are only two ways a passenger and a driver meet at an airport: the driver comes inside and holds a sign, or the passenger walks out and finds the car. They cost different amounts, they fail in different ways, and the customer must choose.

Meet & greet

The driver parks, walks to arrivals and waits at the barrier with a name board. The passenger does not have to find anything.

Costs more — parking plus the driver's time, usually a fixed fee. Ask for the exact spelling of the name that goes on the board. Best for first-time visitors, VIPs, international arrivals, elderly or unaccompanied passengers, and anyone arriving somewhere unfamiliar.

Kerbside

The driver waits in the cell lot and comes to a designated pickup point when the passenger calls or texts on landing.

Cheaper and often faster for a frequent traveller with hand luggage. Depends entirely on the passenger's phone working. Fails badly with international arrivals whose phones are not connected.

Ask; do not assume, and do not default silently

A meet & greet added without being asked for is an unexpected charge on the invoice. A kerbside pickup assumed for a nervous first-time international arrival is a passenger lost in a terminal. The question takes four seconds: "Would you like the driver to meet them inside with a name board, or wait for a call at the kerb?"

What the driver needs, either way

Meet & greetKerbside
The exact name for the board, spelled outThe passenger's mobile, confirmed reachable on landing
Terminal and the specific arrivals hallThe pickup zone the airport designates
Whether the passenger knows to look for a boardWhether the passenger knows to call on landing, and which number
The flight, for the driver's own timingThe flight, so the driver can be in the cell lot in time

When they cannot find each other

1Establish where each of them physically isNot "has the driver arrived" — which door, which level, which terminal. Most connection failures are two people in the same building on different floors.
2Give each one the other's location in plain words"He's at the barrier by exit 3 in Terminal 5 arrivals, holding a board with your name."
3Offer to connect them, per client procedureSome clients allow you to bridge the call or share the driver's number; some do not. Know which before you need it.
4Stay on it until they are togetherDo not close the interaction on "they should find each other now". Confirm the pickup happened.
5Escalate if it runs longTen minutes of failed connection at an airport, or any hint the passenger is vulnerable or distressed, is an escalation.
Lesson 5 of 5

8.5 Knowledge check

Knowledge check

Airport transportation

Pass mark: 4 of 5.

A caller books an arrival and says "he lands about 2:30, so make it 3 o'clock". What should you do?

A hand-typed time does not move. Tying the pickup to the flight is the whole reason for collecting a flight number, and it is what the customer actually wants even though they asked for a clock time.

A passenger is arriving from Frankfurt into a US airport. The client's standard domestic clearance allowance is 40 minutes. What do you use?

International arrivals clear immigration and customs. Using a domestic allowance leaves the driver waiting, running up wait time, or leaving before the passenger emerges.

A booked flight is diverted to another airport. What is the correct response?

Monitoring moves times; it cannot move a car to a different city. A diversion is an operational exception that needs a person and usually an escalation.

Which airport situation is the most dangerous precisely because it is quiet?

Loud problems get attention. An early landing or a silently changed flight produces no alert and no complaint until a passenger is standing alone in a terminal.

A first-time international visitor is arriving and the caller has not specified how the driver should meet them. What do you do?

Both silent defaults cause failures — an unexpected charge, or a lost passenger with no roaming. Ask, explain the trade-off in one sentence, and record the answer.
Phase 3 · Reservation & product knowledge

Rates, charges & policies

≡ Syllabus · Phase 3 · Module 9
≈ 20 min
≡Definition

A price has two parts: a base, which comes from a rate table, and a stack of add-ons — gratuity, tax, fees, tolls, wait time — which calculate on top of it in a defined order.

You are not setting rates. You are explaining them, applying them correctly, and knowing which ones you may not change.

»Example

"Why is it $211 when you quoted $150?" — $150 base, $30 gratuity at 20%, $14.85 tax, $6.15 fuel surcharge, $10 airport fee. Every line is explainable. None of them is negotiable by you.

✓Key points
  • Four base models: flat, hourly, distance, per passenger
  • Hourly minimums gate availability — they do not round up
  • Add-ons stack in an order the client configures
  • Cancellation and no-show charges are policy, and policy is not yours to waive
9.1 How a price is built9.2 The add-ons9.3 Wait time, grace, can…9.4 Knowledge check
Lesson 1 of 4

9.1 How a price is built

How trips get priced

ModelHow it worksTypical use
Fixed (zone-to-zone)A pre-set price from zone A to zone B for a vehicle class. Zones are cities/zip groups or airports.Airport transfers, well-known routes
HourlyRate × hours, with a minimum number of hours per vehicle type. Below the minimum the vehicle is unavailable, not rounded up.As-directed, events, weddings
DistancePer-mile / per-km, usually tiered ("first mile $65, next 10 at $2, remaining at $1.50") so short trips still hit a minimum.Coverage outside your fixed-rate zones
PassengerRate × number of passengers. Switched on per vehicle type with Calculate Rates Based On → Passengers.Shuttles, coaches
Fixed-or-distanceLook for a fixed rate first; if no zone pair exists, fall back to distance.Common on point-to-point and airport work

On top of the base come gratuity (20% is the industry norm), taxes, surcharges (fuel, STC), tolls/parking, wait time, extra stops and discounts. How those calculate against one another is a configuration decision — Section 06 covers it.

Lesson 2 of 4

9.2 The add-ons: what goes on top of the base

The base is only the start. These are the lines that appear beneath it, roughly in the order they usually calculate.

LineWhat it isWhat to tell a customer
GratuityDriver's tip, typically 20% of the base. Often included automatically on corporate accounts.Say whether it is already included. The commonest billing dispute is a customer tipping again because nobody said.
TaxWhere it applies it is configured per company — as a percentage rate or a miscellaneous fee rather than a built-in line — so the label differs between operators. Usually calculated on the base and often not on the gratuity.Non-negotiable and not the operator's money. Read the exact name off the client's own rate lines.
Fuel surchargeA percentage covering fuel cost volatility.A standing charge, not a one-off penalty.
Airport feeWhat the airport charges for commercial vehicle access, passed through.Charged by the airport, not the operator.
Tolls and parkingActual costs incurred, added after the ride from the driver's report.These are why a final invoice can exceed a quote. Say so at quote time.
Wait timeBillable waiting beyond the grace period, charged per hour or part hour.Explain the grace period at booking, especially on airport work.
Additional stopsA per-stop charge, and possibly wait time at the stop.Ask about stops when booking so this is never a surprise.
Meet & greetA fixed fee for the driver parking and meeting inside.Only when asked for. Never added silently.
Child seatsOften a per-seat charge.Confirm availability before promising, not just price.
Discounts and promo codesAccount-negotiated rates or a code. Applied by the system, not by you.If a customer claims a rate you cannot see, do not improvise — escalate.

How the stack calculates

Order matters. A surcharge calculated on the base is a different number from one calculated on the running total.

Flat rate (base)DFW → downtown, SUV150.00
Extra stop1 × 10.0010.00
Gratuity20% × base 160.0032.00
State tax8.25% × base 160.00 — not on the tip13.20
Fuel surcharge3% × (160 + 32 + 13.20)6.16
Airport feeflat10.00
Grand total221.36
You explain the stack; you do not rebuild it

If a customer disputes a line, read it back to them from the trip and route the dispute to accounting. Recalculating a price by hand to "check" it produces a second number, and now there are two figures in play and one of them is yours.

Lesson 3 of 4

9.3 Wait time, grace, cancellation and no-show

Wait time and grace

Local pickup

Grace typically 15 minutes from the scheduled pickup time. After that, wait time bills per hour or part hour at a published rate.

Airport arrival

Grace typically 30–60 minutes from actual landing, not from the scheduled pickup, to cover immigration and baggage. International allowances are longer.

Say the grace period at booking

One sentence — "there's 45 minutes' free waiting from when the flight lands, after that it's charged" — prevents the most common billing argument in the industry. It also gives the passenger a reason to keep their phone on.

Cancellation

Every client sets their own windows. The shape is almost always a ladder by vehicle class and notice given.

Notice givenTypical sedan / SUVTypical larger vehicle
More than 24 hoursNo chargeNo charge, or deposit retained
4–24 hoursNo charge, or a partial chargePartial to full charge
Under 4 hoursOften full chargeFull charge
Driver already en route or on locationFull chargeFull charge
Never quote a cancellation charge from memory

Read it from the client's policy, or say you will confirm it. An agent who guesses low creates a dispute for accounting; an agent who guesses high loses the client a customer. "Let me confirm the exact figure for you" is always an acceptable answer.

No-show

A no-show is the car present, waiting out the grace, and no passenger. It normally bills in full — and it is almost never a decision an agent makes alone.

1Confirm the car was actually there, on time, in the right placeCheck the driver's status and location. A "no-show" that was a car at the wrong terminal is a service failure, not a no-show.
2Confirm contact was attemptedDid the driver call the passenger? Did anyone call the arranger? Document what was tried and when.
3Wait out the full grace period before anyone leavesReleasing a car early turns a billable no-show into an unbillable failure.
4Escalate the decisionWhether to declare and bill a no-show is a client decision. Present the facts; do not announce the outcome to the customer.
The one thing you never do

Waive, discount, or promise a refund. Not for a valued account, not to calm an angry caller, not "just this once". Record the request, route it to the person who can authorise it, and tell the customer honestly that you have done so.

Lesson 4 of 4

9.4 Knowledge check

Knowledge check

Rates, charges and policies

Pass mark: 3 of 4.

A customer asks why their $150 quote became a $221 invoice. What is the right approach?

Every line is explainable from the record. Recalculating by hand introduces a second figure; offering a reduction is not yours to give.

A vehicle type has a four-hour hourly minimum and a customer wants it for two hours. What happens?

A minimum is a condition of availability, not a rounding rule. The vehicle is filtered out, and the customer is offered an alternative or a quote request.

A driver reports the passenger never appeared. Before anything is billed as a no-show, what must be established?

A "no-show" where the car was at the wrong terminal is a service failure. Establish the facts, document the attempts, wait the grace, and let the client make the call.

A long-standing corporate account asks you to waive a late-cancellation charge. What is the correct response?

You neither grant it nor refuse it on the client's behalf. You route it, honestly and promptly, to the person whose decision it is.

Limo Anywhere at a glance

Limo Anywhere is a cloud-based back office for chauffeured transportation companies — reservations, dispatch, driver app, online booking, payments, invoicing, payroll and reports, all from one login.

A two-car operator in Dallas logs in at manage.mylimobiz.com, takes a phone booking, sends it to a driver's phone, charges the card and pays the driver — without leaving the browser.

10.1 The product family

The product family

Core

Back office (LA Core)

The browser app you will live in: manage.mylimobiz.com (or limoanywhere.com/login). Reservations, dispatch, accounts, settings, reports.

Customer-facing

ORES & Passenger Web App

ORES is the Online REServation System — the booking widget embedded on the operator's website, plus a mobile-first PWA. Customers self-book, request quotes and manage their account.

Driver-facing

Driver Anywhere

iOS/Android app where drivers accept offers, run status updates, track GPS, take pictures and even payments. Must be enabled per driver.

Ops

Limo Anywhere Mobile

Dispatcher's mobile app for managing the board on the go.

Network

LA Net & Partner Network

Farm trips in and out to other LA operators with real-time status sync; partner integrations with GroundSpan, GRiDD, Boston Coach and others.

Money

LAPA (LA Pay)

Integrated card processing. Tokenised cards, payment requests by email/SMS, batch payments at settlement. Stripe/Square outside the US.

Lesson 2 of 7

10.2 Packages: Core, Plus and Black

Packages: Core, Plus and Black

LA Core

The base system

Ideal for operators managing up to 500 trips per month. Reservations, dispatch, accounts, rates and reporting — the features this academy teaches. Core also includes three free add-ons an administrator activates from the add-on icons: Manifest Upload, Vehicle Maintenance Management and Incident Management.

LA Plus

Add-ons bundle

Ideal for operators managing up to 1,500 trips per month — the most popular plan. Everything in Core plus extra automation. Upgraded from the add-ons dashboard ("Upgrade to Plus") by an administrator who signs the terms.

LA Black

Top tier

For higher-volume and more automated operations. Adds features such as Auto Farm, GPS provider integration, surveys and driver/vehicle sync. Black operators show a badge in LA Net affiliate searches — a signal of higher automation.

3 · Password

Drivers log in differently

Lesson 4 of 7

10.4 Knowledge check: the product

Knowledge check 02

Product overview

Pass mark: 3 of 4.

A new driver was added yesterday but "could not log you in" appears in Driver Anywhere. Most likely cause?

Saving a driver does not enable the app. The operator must turn on the Driver Anywhere settings for that driver.

Which of these is the customer-facing booking widget?

ORES = Online Reservation System. LA Net is the affiliate network; LAPA is payments.

Where is a user's Company ID found?

For security the company ID is left out of the invite; the admin shares it.

Why does typing "DFW" in the airport field and tabbing away fail to price a trip?

The rate lookup matches on the stored code. Free text in the box is just text until you pick a result.

Customer & account management

≡ Syllabus · Phase 4 · Module 11
≈ 15 min
≡Definition

An account is the customer record everything hangs off: rates, billing terms, standing instructions, history. Attaching a trip to the right account is what makes the rest of the reservation behave correctly.

Attaching it to a new account that should not exist is the most common and most expensive data error an agent makes.

»Example

Vertex Group has negotiated rates and direct billing. An agent types "Vertex Grp" as a fresh account. The trip prices at retail, invoices to nobody, and next month someone has to merge two customer histories by hand.

✓Key points
  • Search before you create — always, every time
  • Search three ways before concluding it does not exist
  • Read the account notes before you speak again
  • Billing, booking and passenger are three roles on one trip

11.1 The "who" column and the account model

≡Definition

An account is a person, not a company. It can play three roles — billing contact (pays), booking contact (calls), passenger (rides). People at one company are linked only by an identical Company Name.

»Example

Jonathan (billing + booking + passenger, company "Corn") and Brian (passenger only, company "Corn"). Brian's trips can bill to Jonathan because the company names match exactly.

✓Key points
  • Account #, Billing Contact and Company Name are one search box with three labels
  • Typing 3 letters shows matches — click one to attach the account
  • Typing a name and tabbing away stores text only: no history, no cards, no rates
  • Attached correctly, the passenger icon lists that account's riders

What attaching an account brings in

Cards on file (from billing contact and passenger), account-specific rates in the ACCT tab, default payment method and terms, stored addresses, account notes, and the trip in the account's history.

Ad-hoc callers

Someone with no account can still be typed in as billing contact and passenger. Fine for one-offs; use Create New Acct if they will book again.

Why duplicates hurt

A second account for the same person splits their history, cards and rates in two, and someone has to merge them later by hand. Search first, create last.

Rule of thumb

Search, then select. If you clear the account with the CL button, both the account number and the billing contact go — they cannot exist without each other. Enter the passenger's mobile number: automated "driver on the way" texts go to that field.

Lesson 2 of 3

11.2 Finding the right account, and not making a second one

In plain words — Duplicate accounts are created by agents in a hurry who searched once, found nothing, and typed a new record. The fix is a habit: three searches before you create anything.

Search three ways

1Phone numberThe single most reliable key. People change companies and spell their names differently; their mobile stays the same. Try it with and without formatting.
2Last name, partialType three or four letters, not the whole name. "Whit" finds Whitfield, Whitford and Whittaker — and it finds the one someone typed as "Whitfeild".
3Company name, partial"Vert" finds Vertex Group, Vertex Grp and Vertex Group Inc. If you find more than one, you have found a duplicate somebody else created — flag it rather than adding a third.
Then, if it is genuinely new, create it properly

Full legal-ish company name, the contact's full name spelled correctly, a working email, a mobile. A record created in thirty seconds with "J Smith" and no email is a record the next agent will not find, and will duplicate.

Which account is the right one

Finding a match is not the same as finding the right match. Confirm before you attach.

Check the history

"I have you at the Fairmont on Tuesday — is that the one?" A caller who says "no, that's a different Dana" has just saved you an hour.

Check the company

Two people with the same name at different companies are two accounts. Two people with the same name at the same company are usually one account someone duplicated.

Check it is not an affiliate record

Partner operators appear as accounts too, flagged as affiliates. A trip attached to an affiliate account by mistake prices against affiliate terms.

Check it is active

Some clients disable accounts that have gone to collections or left. An inactive account is an escalation, not a booking.

What to read before you speak again

Account notes are where the client keeps everything you would otherwise learn by getting it wrong.

You will findWhich changes
"Always confirm with the assistant, never call the passenger"Who you contact on the day, and who gets the confirmation
"Premium sedan only for Mr Adeyemi"The vehicle type, regardless of what fits
"Direct bill, net 30 — do not take a card"The payment method
"Meet & greet standard on all arrivals"The airport arrangement and the price
"Two failed pickups — flag any issue to operations immediately"Your escalation threshold for this account
Notes you add belong in the right place

Anything that is true of this customer forever goes on the account. Anything true only of this trip goes on the reservation. A standing instruction typed onto one trip vanishes the moment that trip is settled.

Lesson 3 of 3

11.3 Knowledge check

Knowledge check

Customer and account management

Pass mark: 3 of 4.

You search a caller's surname, find nothing, and need to book quickly. What next?

Three searches: phone, partial surname, partial company. A name search alone misses every record where the name was typed slightly differently.

Searching "Vert" returns both "Vertex Group" and "Vertex Grp". What should you do?

One of them is the real account with the rates and terms. Using the wrong one misprices the trip; creating a third makes the problem worse.

An account note reads "always confirm with the assistant, never call the passenger". A driver cannot find the passenger at the kerb. What do you do?

Standing preferences govern routine contact. A live connection failure is an exception, and the client's procedure for it — not your own judgement and not the routine note — is what applies.

Where does "this customer always wants a premium sedan" belong?

It is true of the customer, not of one trip. On a reservation it disappears when that trip is settled.

12.1 Anatomy of the screen

The system only requires three things — but that is not the standard you work to

Limo Anywhere will let you save with just a billing contact, a PU date and a PU time. (Some companies add "payment method" as a fourth requirement in preferences.) Knowing this is not permission to use it. A reservation that saves is not the same as a reservation that can be driven: without a pickup address, a destination, a vehicle type and a passenger mobile number, nobody can run that trip. Treat the three as what the database insists on, and the fifteen fields in Module 7 as what you actually collect. If you ever do save a partial booking, the gap is yours to close before the day.

Every click of New Res generates the next sequential confirmation number immediately — the yellow banner reminds you it exists but is not saved. Close without saving and it lands in Reservations › Unfinalized.

Required by the system

To press Save

  1. Billing contact
  2. PU date
  3. PU time
  4. (Payment method, if your company switched on that requirement)
Required by a good booking

Before you hang up

  1. Passenger name and mobile number (texts go there)
  2. Pick-up and drop-off stored in routing — with flight number for airports
  3. Service type and vehicle type
  4. A rate applied and read back to the caller
  5. Payment method (card on file, new card, or direct bill for accounts)
  6. Passenger count, luggage, child seats, special notes

Save

Top or bottom, same button. Warns about driver/car conflicts but never hard-blocks.

Payments

Record a payment, use a card on file, or send a LAPA payment / card-on-file request link.

Copy · Round Trip

Duplicate once or on a schedule; or create the mirrored return trip.

Email / Fax · Print

Confirmations, trip sheets, custom forms, invoices — to the contacts on the account.

Res log

Field-by-field change history with user, old and new value; add comments; export.

Link

Group reservations and replicate changes across them. Red = links exist.

More ▾

Incident log, Settle, Quote log, Dispatch log, Delete, Unfinalize.

Affiliate: LA Net / Manually

Farm-out buttons in the right column, visible when trip type is Farm-out.

12.3 Routing: pickups, stops, waits and drop-offs

≡Definition

Routing is the list of places on a trip. Each place has a type (Address, Airport, Seaport, FBO, POI) and an action (Pick-up, Drop-off, Stop, Wait).

»Example

Airport tab → DFW, AA 3211 → click Pick-up. Address tab → 1104 Cotton Exchange Dr → click Drop-off. Both now sit in Stored Routing Information.

✓Key points
  • Pick the tab, enter the place, then click the action
  • The action is what stores it — clicking Pick-up on an empty form errors
  • Select Google's standardised address; typed-as-is addresses get no mileage
  • One trip = one pick-up, optional stops/waits, one drop-off

Address

Type street and city; Google verifies it and adds zip and country. Pick the standardised match — "use as originally entered" gets no mileage.

Airport

Stored Airports are your favourites (enabled under Company Resources). Add airline + flight number: arrivals sync the spot time to the flight; departures are informational.

POI · FBO · Seaport

Stored venues, private-jet terminals and cruise ports with their own lists. Many agents type a venue name in the Address tab instead and let Google find it.

Stop vs Wait

Both are places between pick-up and drop-off. A Wait carries a time so wait-time charges can apply.

One trip = one route

Several passengers on different flights cannot be tracked on one reservation — make one per flight and give them the same driver. Multi-leg days are separate reservations (lesson 4.12).

Time In ≠ pick-up time

The Time In field on a routing item is a note, not the pickup. The times that matter are PU date/time, DO time and spot time at the top.

12.4 Service type → vehicle type → price

≡Definition

Pricing is a chain: the service type decides how to price and which vehicle types are offered; the vehicle type decides which cars fit; only then can Apply Rate Table look up a price.

»Example

From Airport (Fixed-or-Distance) → SUV → Apply Rate Table → FIXED (1): DFW → SVN $165 → click it → Grand Total $203.94.

✓Key points
  • Prices are never applied on Save — open the rate book and click
  • Tabs show a count of rates found for this trip
  • Zero out leftover values from an earlier lookup
  • You can also type straight into the line items
1Service typee.g. From Airport → pricing type Fixed-or-Distance
2Vehicle typeOnly types associated with that service type are listed
3Apply Rate TableFIXED · HRLY (also per-pax) · ACCT · PROMO · MISC · DIST — a count shows what was found
4Click a rateValues drop into the line items; totals recalculate. Zero out anything left over.
5Driver & carOptional here; a car that doesn't match the vehicle type warns but does not block

Tour 2 · The real rate window

Hourly trips

Duration defaults to 1 hour. Updating the DO time updates duration, but not the other way round. With the "auto-populate number of hours" preference on, the duration flows into the Per Hour multiplier; otherwise type it. Rate lookups with the wrong duration produce nonsense like 0.03 × $350.

Tested in the demo system

With no service type chosen, the Vehicle Type dropdown offered 11 vehicles. Selecting From Airport reduced it to 7 — 15 Passenger Van, the 8-passenger stretch, Minibus and Motor Coach all dropped out, because none of them is associated with that service type. Nothing was saved and nothing was announced; the list simply changed. If a customer insists a vehicle "was available last time", this is usually why.

So when a vehicle is missing, check these in order

1Service typeIs the right one selected? Changing it re-filters the vehicle list immediately.
2The associationMy Office›Company Resources›Vehicle Types › open the vehicle › Associated With Service Types. If the service type is not ticked there, the vehicle will never appear for it.
3StatusAn INACTIVE vehicle type is hidden everywhere.
4Hourly minimumOn an hourly booking below the minimum, the vehicle is filtered out rather than rounded up.
5RateA vehicle with no matching rate for this trip can appear with no price, which is a different problem — see the rate tabs above.

12.5 Payment info: how the trip gets paid

≡Definition

The Payment Info tab records how this trip will be paid. It never takes money — charging happens through the Payments action in the toolbar.

»Example

Priya’s account is Direct Bill/Invoice, so Payment Method defaults to that and no card is needed. A walk-in caller instead needs a card entered or requested before Save will go through.

✓Key points
  • Defaults come from the account’s Financial Data tab
  • Direct Bill/Invoice is only offered when a real account is attached
  • Cards are tokenised — you see only the last four digits
  • Company Preferences can make a card required to save

Payment Info tab

Beside "Bill To & Pax". Payment method (defaults from the account), cards from the billing contact's or passenger's account, a new card, PO / voucher numbers. Direct Bill/Invoice is only available when a real account is attached. Taking or requesting a payment happens via the Payments action.

Taking the money

Nothing is charged from this tab. Payments in the toolbar charges a card or records cash/cheque; Send payment request emails the customer a secure page where they type their own card — the safest way to take a card over the phone. Deposits and part-payments show up as Payments/Deposits against the Grand Total.

Lesson 6 of 12

12.6 Notes: four kinds, and who reads them

≡Definition

A note is free text attached to a trip. Which box you type it in decides who sees it — and one of those audiences is the customer.

»Example

“Meet at door D22” belongs in trip notes (the customer reads it). “VIP, do not chat” belongs in Dispatch Notes (internal). Both on the same trip.

✓Key points
  • Trip notes print on confirmations — the customer sees them
  • Dispatch Notes are internal; Partner Notes go to an affiliate
  • Bill To & Pax notes come from the account and repeat on every trip
  • A routing note belongs to one stop; Add to T/S puts it on the trip sheet

Tour · The four places a note can live

Where each one ends up

The four note boxes, as the screen labels them

On the reservation you will find Trip Notes and Bill To & Pax Notes as tabs, and Dispatch Notes and Partner Notes beneath them. Two checkboxes sit alongside: Add to T/S puts the note on the trip sheet, and Hide From Customer keeps it off anything the customer receives. Read the labels — customers see some of these.

Read the label before you type

The single most common note mistake is putting an internal comment where the customer will read it. If you are not sure which box you are in, look at the label above it — and when in doubt, put it in driver / dispatch notes, which nobody outside the company ever sees.

12.7 Extras: passengers, signs, seats and labels

≡Definition

The extras are the small fields that decide whether the trip actually goes right on the day — and the ones you can report on afterwards.

»Example

Three passengers, five bags, an infant seat and a booster, a greeting sign reading NAIR / FULL STEAM, group name “FullSteam Q3 offsite”.

✓Key points
  • Only the primary passenger gets automated messages
  • Pax and luggage counts are checked against vehicle capacity
  • Child-seat count multiplies the child-seat line item
  • Occasion, Source, Group and Arranged-by are reporting fields

Additional passengers

Add names and emails for the manifest. Only the primary passenger receives automated messages, but many corporate clients require every rider recorded.

Greeting sign, child seats, luggage

Greeting sign text for meet-and-greet; child seat required + count (multiplies the child-seat line item); passenger and luggage counts checked against vehicle capacity.

Occasion · Source · Group · Arranged by

Free-text lists you can report on later: what the trip was for, how the customer found you, a group name that ties 10 wedding cars together. Managed under My Office › List Management.

Read-back script

A pop-up on first (or every) save that reads the booking back to the caller — passenger, date, time, PU/DO, fare, payment method — in bold from live data. Templates per service type under My Office › Company Settings › Read Back Script; turned on in Company Preferences › Reservations.

Lesson 8 of 12

12.8 Putting a driver and a car on the trip

≡Definition

Choosing a driver and a car on the reservation is a plan. It writes two names on the trip. It sends nothing, tells nobody, and the trip stays Unassigned on the board.

»Example

Pick Darrell in the Driver list and Sedan3 in the Car list, press Save — Darrell’s phone stays silent. Only a status change dispatches him (next lesson).

✓Key points
  • Driver, Preferred Driver and Car are three different fields
  • A car that does not match the vehicle type warns, it does not block
  • Primary and Secondary tabs let two cars run one trip
  • Assigning here is optional — dispatch can do it later on the board

Driver vs Preferred Driver

Driver is who is actually doing this trip. Preferred Driver is a note of who the customer likes — it is used when dispatch is deciding, and it can be defaulted from the account so it appears on every booking.

Car ≠ vehicle type

Vehicle type is what was sold (Sedan, SUV). The car is a specific vehicle in the fleet. Picking a car outside the sold type raises a warning so you can catch “we sold an SUV and put a sedan on it” before the passenger does.

Two cars, one trip

Eight passengers and one sedan? Either book two reservations, or use the Secondary tab to add a second driver and car to this trip. Secondary has its own rate section so the extra car can be priced.

The trap

New agents put a driver on and tell the customer “you’re all set, Darrell will be there”. Darrell knows nothing about it. Until the status changes, nothing has left the office.

Lesson 9 of 12

12.9 Copy and recurring trips

≡Definition

Copy makes a new reservation from an existing one — same passenger, routing and rates, a new date and a new confirmation number. It can also generate a whole recurring series in one press.

»Example

A school run every weekday until 20 December: open the trip, Copy, frequency Every workday, End by 20 Dec, email confirmations off, Copy Reservation.

✓Key points
  • Every copy gets its own confirmation number
  • Frequency + end condition build a recurring series
  • Turn confirmations off when generating many
  • What carries over is set in Company Preferences › Reservations

Copy

From the open reservation click Copy. Change any field (date, vehicle, service, driver), tick or untick Send email confirmations, Link copy to original and Copy affiliate rate data, then Copy Reservation. For a recurring trip set the next date, a frequency (daily / every N days / workdays / weekly…), and an end — after N occurrences or on a date. Leave confirmations off when generating dozens. What is carried over is governed by Company Preferences › Reservations.

“Same as last time”

The everyday case: find last week’s trip (Dispatch › right-click › Copy, or open it and press Copy), change the date, End After 1 occurrence, done. Check the driver and car — a copy keeps them, which is right for next Tuesday and wrong for next March.

Tour · The Copy dialog

Continuation trips: one passenger, several legs in a day

EXAMPLEThe itinerary09:00 DFW → hotel · 13:00 hotel → client office · 19:00 office → restaurant → hotel
RULEOne leg = one reservationEach leg with its own start time is a separate reservation, never extra stops on the first one. Stops are for pauses within a leg (the restaurant).
HOWCopy the first legSave leg 1, press Copy, change time and routing, keep the same driver and car, tick Link copy to original. Repeat for leg 3.
WHYSeparate legs give you…a status per leg on Dispatch, correct pricing per leg, flight tracking on the airport leg, and Replicate Changes across the linked set if the passenger's details change.
Or make it hourly

If the client wants the car all day at their disposal, book one hourly / as-directed reservation for the block instead of separate legs — the rate is per hour and the drop-off is optional.

Lesson 10 of 12

12.10 Round trips and continuation trips

≡Definition

A round trip is the return leg, created from a saved outbound trip with the pick-up and drop-off already swapped. It is a second reservation, not a second half of the first one.

»Example

Home → DFW on 16 Sep (Conf# 15501). Round Trip → DFW → Home on 19 Sep with flight AA 1180 (Conf# 15502), linked to the first.

✓Key points
  • Save the outbound first — Round Trip needs a saved trip
  • You must ask for the return date and time
  • An airport return needs its own airline and flight number
  • Two confirmation numbers, each with its own rate, driver and status

Round trip — step by step

  1. Book and save the outbound trip first (e.g. home → DFW, 11:00).
  2. Click Round Trip in the toolbar.
  3. Ask the caller: "What date and time do you want to come back?" Enter the return PU date/time; for an airport return add the inbound flight.
  4. PU and DO are already swapped. Tick Link to original so both trips reference each other on paperwork.
  5. Email confirmations now or later. Press Create. You now have two confirmation numbers; the return has its own rate, driver and status.

Why not one long trip?

Because a trip has one pick-up time, one driver, one status and one price. A return three days later shares none of those. Two reservations let dispatch run them independently and let the customer be charged correctly for each.

12.11 Linking trips and Replicate Changes

≡Definition

A link is an operational relationship between reservations. Once trips are linked, Replicate Changes can push a correction from one of them onto all the others in a single press.

»Example

Ten trips were booked without the account attached. Fix one, link the other nine to it, tick “bill-to / passenger”, Replicate Information — all ten now bill correctly.

✓Key points
  • Links are always to the reservation you started from
  • The Linked Reservations tab unlinks; Link Reservations searches for trips to add
  • You choose exactly which data points get pushed
  • There is no undo

Linking groups reservations so you can see them together and update them in one go. Click Link (red when links already exist). The Linked Reservations tab lists the group — tick and Remove Link Between Selected to unlink. The Link Reservations tab lists every unsettled trip in the system; search by field and date range, tick, then Link Selected. Links are always to the reservation you started from, so link each new trip from that same one.

Replicate Changes is the payoff. Edit one reservation, click Link › Replicate Changes, choose all linked or only selected, tick the data points to push — bill-to / booked-by / passenger, pickup date and times, routing, pax and luggage counts, notes, rates, service and vehicle type, driver and car, contact info, seats, referral source, payment method, rental agreement — and press Replicate Information. Typical use: ten trips booked without the account attached; fix one, link the rest, replicate the billing contact. There is no undo.

Group name vs. link

A group name (right column) is a label for reporting — "Smith wedding" pulls all ten cars into one report. A link is an operational relationship that lets you replicate changes. Linking also prints a "linked to #…" note on paperwork; it changes no pricing or dispatch logic.

Lesson 12 of 12

12.12 Knowledge check

Knowledge check 04

Reservation process

Pass mark: 6 of 9.

You typed "Brandon Edley" in Billing Contact and tabbed to the next field without clicking a search result. Later you look at Brandon's account history. The trip is…

The billing-contact field is a search. Selecting a result attaches the account; typing does not.

A caller wants an SUV from DFW to downtown. You entered the airport but the "Pick-up" button gives an error. Why?

Enter the location, then click Pick-up / Drop-off / Stop / Wait to store it.

You selected a driver and car on the reservation and saved. What does the driver see in Driver Anywhere?

Naming a driver only records it. The status change is the dispatch action.

A web customer requested a quote. What converts it into a reservation without you taking payment by phone?

The convert link in the emailed quote takes the customer to a payment page; the quote converts itself.

You set a trip to Farm-out, chose the affiliate and clicked LA Net, but got "please set the trip to farm out". What did you skip?

The farm-out type and affiliate must be saved on the record before the LA Net action can read them.

Ten reservations for one client were entered without the account attached. Fastest fix?

Link groups them; Replicate pushes the corrected billing contact to all linked trips. Group name is only a report label.

An affiliate accepted your LA Net farm-out but their driver's "On the way" never shows on your board. Most likely?

Real-time LA Net updates require the setting to be Yes on both sides.

A client needs 09:00 airport → hotel, 13:00 hotel → office and 19:00 office → hotel, same day. How do you book it?

Each leg with its own start time is its own reservation; stops are only for pauses within one leg. Linking keeps them together.

A trip was settled yesterday and the driver now reports a $12 toll that was never added. What do you do?

Settled trips are locked. Reopen is the deliberate, logged way to correct one.
Phase 5 · Last-minute requests & operational changes

Last-minute customer requests & changes

≡ Syllabus · Phase 5 · Module 13
≈ 20 min
≡Definition

A last-minute change is any change close enough to the pickup that a car, a driver, or another customer's trip may already be committed to it. Changing the record is easy. Changing the operation is the part that needs checking.

The nearer the pickup, the less of the decision is yours.

»Example

"Can we make it 6am instead of 8?" — at 48 hours' notice, a two-second edit. At 22:00 the night before, that driver has a 5am job, the car is fifty miles away, and moving it breaks two other trips. Same words, different problem.

✓Key points
  • Check the impact before you confirm, not after
  • Saving a change does not tell a driver anything
  • Anything inside a few hours is an operations decision
  • Never say yes on the operator's behalf to something they may not be able to do
13.1 After it's booked13.2 The impact check, bef…13.3 Same-day and immediat…13.4 Knowledge check
Lesson 1 of 4

13.1 After it's booked: changes and settled trips

In plain words — Customers change their minds: a new flight, a different hotel, one more passenger. Changing a saved reservation is normal and easy. The one state you must respect is settled — that means the trip has been closed and the money and pay recorded, so changing it is a deliberate, logged action.

Making a change to a live reservation

1Find itType the confirmation number in Find (top bar), or right-click the row on Dispatch › Detailed Edit, or search Reservations / the account's History.
2Edit and SaveChange the field — time, routing, vehicle, passenger, rate. Re-apply the rate table if the change affects price. Save.
3Tell the people affectedCustomer: Email/Fax › confirmation again (it isn't automatic). Driver: if already assigned, they see the updated details in the app; change the driver or status if the plan changed. Affiliate: LA Net farm-outs sync; manual ones need an email.
4Check the trailThe Res log records who changed what, old and new value. Use it when "someone changed my booking".

Changing many at once

Same passenger, five trips this week, new phone number? Link them and use Replicate Changes (lesson 4.13). For a whole account, edit the account and the next bookings pick it up.

Cancelling

Change the status to your Cancelled (or Late cancelled / No show) status — never delete. Cancelled trips keep their history, can carry a cancellation fee, and still need settling. Send the cancellation email from Email/Fax.

Deleting

More › Delete is for true mistakes (a test booking, a duplicate). It asks for the master delete password and the trip moves to Reservations › Deleted.

What "settled" means

DONETrip finishedStatus mapped to Completed (or cancelled). It now appears under the Settle icon.
PAIDBalance is zeroPayment taken, or the account is Direct Bill / Invoice. Charges corrected (wait time, tolls, extra stop).
PAYDriver / affiliate / agent pay confirmedWhat each party earns on this trip is recorded on the settle window.
SETTLEDFiledPress Settle. The trip is locked: it feeds driver payroll, affiliate payables and invoices. On Dispatch it shows your settled status.
Changing a settled trip

Reopen, fix, re-settle

  1. Settle icon › Settled Reservations tab (or Find the confirmation number).
  2. Click Details on the row to open the settle window.
  3. Press REOPEN. The trip is unsettled and editable again.
  4. Make the change — a missed toll, wrong gratuity, wrong driver pay. If the balance changes, take or refund the difference.
  5. Press UPDATE to save, or SETTLE to file it again.
Before you reopen

Think about what already left

If a driver payroll log, an affiliate pay entry or an invoice has already been generated from this trip, your change will not flow into it automatically — tell accounting so they can regenerate or adjust. Reopening is meant for corrections ("settled in error"), not routine edits. Every reopen is logged.

Lesson 2 of 4

13.2 The impact check, before you say yes

In plain words — Before you agree to a change, ask one question: could this affect anything other than this reservation? If the answer is yes or maybe, you check first and confirm second.

The seven impact checks

1Driver availabilityIs a driver already assigned, and does the new time still work for them? A driver with a 05:00 start cannot also do a 04:30.
2Vehicle availabilityIs the vehicle class still free at the new time? A change of vehicle type is a fresh availability question, not an edit.
3Driver assignmentIf someone has accepted this job, they are holding the old details. A saved change they have not been told about is worse than no change.
4Other scheduled ridesMoving this trip may collide with the next one on the same car. Dispatch sees that; the reservation screen does not.
5Affiliate arrangementsIf it is farmed out, the change has to reach another company. That is a phone call and a confirmation, not a field edit.
6PricingA new route, a new vehicle, a new service type or added stops re-price the trip. Tell the customer before they see it on an invoice.
7Timing against policyA change this close may itself carry a charge, or count as a cancellation and rebook. Read the policy; do not guess.

How much of the decision is yours

Notice before pickupWhat you do
More than 24 hoursNormally yours. Make the change, re-price if needed, reconfirm, document.
4–24 hoursMake the change, then actively notify dispatch and the driver. Do not rely on the system.
Under 4 hoursCheck with dispatch before confirming to the customer. "Let me check we can do that and come straight back to you."
Driver en route or on locationOperations decision. Escalate immediately; do not agree to anything.
Farmed out, any noticeConfirm with the affiliate before confirming to the customer. Their acceptance is what makes it real.
The sentence that buys you the check

"Let me just make sure we can cover that at the new time and I'll come straight back to you — two minutes." It costs nothing, it is true, and it stops you promising something the operation cannot deliver. A customer told "yes" and then "actually, no" is far more annoyed than one who waited two minutes.

Saving is not telling

This is the single most important thing in the module. Editing a reservation updates the record. It does not, on its own, reach a driver who already has the job on their phone, a dispatcher who already built the day around it, or an affiliate in another city.

Tell dispatch

By the method the client uses — a note, a call, the dispatch board. Every time, for any change inside 24 hours.

Tell the driver

Or confirm dispatch has. "Assume they saw it" is how a driver arrives at the old address.

Tell the customer what will happen

Revised confirmation, new price if any, and who will contact them. Then document all of it.

Lesson 3 of 4

13.3 Same-day and immediate requests

In plain words — A same-day or immediate request is a new booking with the impact check built in. The customer wants a car now, or in two hours. Whether that is possible is not a question the reservation screen answers.

The order of work

1Get the essentials, fastPassenger, mobile, pickup address, destination, number of passengers, bags, when. Six facts, not fifteen — the rest can follow.
2Do not quote a time yet"Let me check what we have available and come straight back to you." Anything else is a promise you cannot keep.
3Check availability with dispatchIs there a car and a driver who can be there? This is a dispatcher's answer, not a screen's.
4Consider the affiliate routeIf the operator has nothing free, the client's procedure may allow farming it out. That is usually an approval, not your call.
5Come back with a real answer"We can have a sedan with you at 3:15" or "I'm sorry, we can't cover that this afternoon." Both are good answers. "Probably" is not.
6Book it and confirm the priceSame-day work may price differently. Say the figure before you take the booking.

What makes same-day work fail

Promising before checking

The single biggest cause. An agent says "yes, about half an hour" to be helpful and creates a failure the operator has to absorb.

Underestimating the drive

The car has to get there. A "30 minutes" that ignores the deadhead from wherever the driver is now is not 30 minutes.

Not warning about traffic

On an immediate airport run at rush hour, say plainly whether the flight is achievable. Customers would rather be told now.

Skipping the mobile number

On a same-day job the driver will almost certainly need to call. Get it first, not last.

Forgetting to document

Same-day bookings are made under pressure and documented least. They are also the ones most likely to be queried.

Not saying no

"We can't cover that" delivered in time is a good service. Delivered at the pickup time, it is a disaster.

Cancellations close to pickup

The mirror image, and the same rules. Confirm which booking, check whether a charge applies from the client's policy, tell the customer plainly, and make sure dispatch and the driver are told — a cancelled trip nobody told the driver about is a car sitting outside an empty address.

Lesson 4 of 4

13.4 Knowledge check

Knowledge check

Last-minute changes

Pass mark: 3 of 4.

At 22:00 a customer asks to move tomorrow's 08:00 pickup to 06:00. A driver is already assigned. What do you do first?

Ten hours' notice with a driver already assigned is inside the range where the change affects the operation. Check, then confirm.

You edit a reservation that a driver has already accepted. What has the driver been told?

Saving updates the record. Assuming it reaches a driver holding the old details is how a car turns up at the old address at the old time.

A customer wants a car "as soon as possible" to catch a flight in two hours during rush hour. What is the right handling?

Neither optimism nor a flat refusal. Get the facts, check, and give the customer a true answer while they still have other options.

A farmed-out trip needs a pickup-time change. When can you confirm it to the customer?

Another company is driving it. Their acceptance is what makes the change real; an unacknowledged email is not a confirmation.
Phase 6 · Quotes, Groups & Events

Standard quotes

≡ Syllabus · Phase 6 · Module 14
≈ 15 min
≡Definition

A quote is a price given without a commitment. No car is held, no driver is allocated, and nothing appears on the dispatch board. It is a sales document with an expiry date.

Quotes that are sent and never followed up are the largest source of lost work in the industry.

»Example

"What would four of us cost from the Ritz to JFK on the 22nd?" — gather exactly what a booking would need, price it, send it with a validity date, and set a follow-up. The gathering is identical; only the commitment differs.

✓Key points
  • Gather the same information you would for a booking
  • Say what is included — especially gratuity and fees
  • Give the quote an expiry
  • Document it and set the follow-up before you move on
14.1 Quotes14.2 Preparing, sending an…14.3 Knowledge check
Lesson 1 of 3

14.1 Quotes: leads that are not yet reservations

≡Definition

A quote is a price request that is not yet a booking — no card, no promise. It lives under the Quotes icon, not on the dispatch board, until it is converted.

»Example

A visitor on the website asks "how much from DFW to Lewisville?" It arrives as quote #15495. You price it, email it; she clicks the link, enters a card, and it becomes reservation #15496.

✓Key points
  • Created from the website, the New Res ▾ arrow, or Rate › Quote
  • Status is locked to Quote
  • Email a Response Template — the convert link is what lets the customer accept
  • Conversion cannot be undone
1Open the requestQuotes › Action › Open Quote Request. Details left, rate toolbar right with counts of matching rates.
2Price itClick a found rate (Fixed, Hourly, Pax, Account, Promo, Misc, Distance) or type into the rate table. Save.
3Email quoteLoad a Response Template, check the merged text, Send and Log Response. Logged in Response/Change Log.
4Customer convertsThey click #CONVERT_LINK#, enter a card, and the quote becomes a live reservation on its own.
5…or you convertConvert icon on the quote toolbar. Then payment is on you to collect. Conversion cannot be reversed.
Which conversion path?

Customer clicks the link when you emailed the quote — they enter their card, the system converts it, you touch nothing. You press Convert when the customer is on the phone saying "book it" — then take the card or payment method yourself right away. Either way the quote number disappears from Quotes and a reservation appears with a Quote log entry.

Response templates

Quotes › Response Templates. Title + text with tags in # marks: #CUST_NAME#, #COMPANY#, #QUOTE_SUMMARY#, #PRICE_QUOTE#, #PHONE#, #EMAIL#, #WEB_ADDRESS#, #RATE_DISCLAIMER# and the essential #CONVERT_LINK# / #CONVERT_URL#. HTML is allowed. An initial response template goes out automatically the moment a web quote arrives.

Quote toolbar

Save · History (response log) · Email · Convert · Exit without saving · Delete. New quote notifications are configured under Quotes › Quote Settings (email / SMS to a named user) — they do not raise the dispatch flag the way online bookings do.

Tour 1 · Emailing the quote

Tour 2 · Quick Rate Lookup — quote or book in one window

Lesson 2 of 3

14.2 Preparing, sending and following up

What a quote must contain

ElementWhy
The date and time, written in fullQuotes are read days later. "Friday 22 September, 2:00pm" leaves no room for reinterpretation.
Pickup and destinationProves you priced the journey they asked about, not a similar one.
Vehicle class, with capacity"SUV (up to 6 passengers, 4–5 large bags)" heads off the "will we fit?" reply.
The total, and what is in itState explicitly whether gratuity, tolls and airport fees are included. This is the line that prevents the invoice dispute.
What is not includedWait time beyond the grace period, extra stops, parking. One sentence.
An alternative, where sensibleOffering a sedan alongside an SUV converts more quotes than a single option.
A validity date"This quote holds until 20 September." Creates a reason to reply.
What you need to book it"Just reply with the passenger's name and mobile and I'll confirm." Makes saying yes a single step.

After you send it

1Record it on the accountWhat was quoted, for what, at what price, and when it expires. The next agent who takes the customer's call needs to see it.
2Set the follow-upPer the client's procedure — typically 48 hours for standard work, sooner for a trip that is close.
3Put it in the handoff if it is still open at end of shiftAn open quote is outstanding work, not finished work.
4Follow up once, usefully"Just checking whether you'd like me to hold the SUV for Friday — happy to confirm it now if so." Not "did you get my email".
5Convert or close itTurn it into a reservation, or mark it declined with a reason. A quote left in limbo is a quote nobody learns from.
Never quote a price you cannot find in the system

If the customer insists on a rate you cannot see, or asks for a discount, that is an escalation and not a negotiation. Quoting a number you invented creates a price the operator is then expected to honour.

Lesson 3 of 3

14.3 Knowledge check

Knowledge check

Standard quotes

Pass mark: 3 of 4.

What is held or reserved when you send a quote?

A quote is a price with no commitment. If the customer accepts a week later, availability is a fresh question.

Which omission from a quote most often causes a dispute later?

A customer who reads $150 and is invoiced $221 will dispute it. Saying what is in the number, and what is not, is the whole prevention.

A customer says another operator quoted less and asks you to match it. What do you do?

You cannot invent a rate, and you should not close the door on the client's behalf. Route it.

A quote you sent yesterday is still unanswered at the end of your shift. What happens to it?

An open quote is unfinished. Quotes that nobody follows up are the biggest single source of lost bookings.
Phase 6 · Quotes, Groups & Events

Groups & event quotes

≡ Syllabus · Phase 6 · Module 15
≈ 25 min
≡Definition

A group or event is any request involving multiple vehicles, multiple movements, or both — a conference shuttle, a wedding, a roadshow, a corporate offsite.

It is not a bigger reservation. It is a small logistics plan, and the operator has to hold real vehicles and real drivers against it, often for months.

»Example

"Forty people arriving Thursday across six flights, hotel shuttle Friday, dinner Saturday, departures Sunday." That is one enquiry and roughly eighteen movements — and it will not price from a rate table.

✓Key points
  • Gather the event, not the trip
  • Movements are the unit of work — count them
  • Everything you produce is preliminary until the operator confirms vehicles
  • Know your handover point, and reach it early
15.1 What makes a group di…15.2 The information a gro…15.3 Building a preliminar…15.4 When to hand it to a…15.5 Knowledge check
Lesson 1 of 5

15.1 What makes a group different

A standard quoteA group / event quote
UnitOne tripMovements — often ten to fifty of them
PricingA rate table lookupBuilt by hand from hours, vehicles and positioning, often with a discount structure
AvailabilityAlmost always fineThe binding constraint. Six coaches on a Saturday in May may simply not exist
CommitmentNone until bookedUsually a deposit and a signed agreement
CancellationHours beforeWeeks before, with a sliding scale
Who prices itYou, from the systemA groups specialist or a senior client contact — almost never you alone
Lead timeMinutesOften days, and legitimately so

Think in movements

A movement is one vehicle going from one place to another at one time. Counting them is how a vague enquiry becomes something that can be planned and priced.

Thursday arrivals40 people, 6 flights, 2 vehicles per wave8 movements
Friday hotel → venue, both ways2 coaches × 24 movements
Saturday dinner, both ways2 coaches × 24 movements
Sunday departuresstaggered, 3 vehicles6 movements
Totalplus positioning and driver hours22 movements
Never quote a group by multiplying a single-trip rate

Forty people is not twenty sedans. It is coaches, hours, waiting, positioning and driver time, and the per-person economics are entirely different. An agent who quotes "about $4,000" from mental arithmetic has created a number the operator will be held to.

Lesson 2 of 5

15.2 The information a group quote needs

Gather all of this before passing it on. A specialist who receives a complete brief can price in an hour; one who receives three lines spends two days asking questions.

The event

What and where

Type of event, the venue or venues with full addresses, and the client's own name for it — groups get referred to by name for months.

Dates and times

Every day involved, and the times that are fixed versus the ones that are flexible. A dinner that must start at 19:00 constrains everything before it.

Total passengers

And how that number splits across days. Forty arriving and twenty-eight departing is normal and changes the plan.

Who is in charge on the day

A named on-site contact with a mobile. Groups without one fail in ways nobody can fix remotely.

The movements

1ArrivalsFlight numbers, times and airports for every inbound. Ask whether they want waves consolidated — six flights can become three vehicles or six.
2Transfers during the eventHotel to venue, venue to dinner. Each one has a time, a direction and a headcount.
3ShuttlesA continuous loop over a period, not a set of trips. Ask for the window and the frequency they want.
4Hourly / as-directed vehiclesCars held for VIPs for a block of time. Note which passengers, which hours.
5DeparturesFlight times drive these backwards. Staggered departures need more vehicles than a single wave.
6LuggageA conference group with checked bags cannot use a coach whose bays are full. Ask.

The commercial facts

Budget

Ask. "Do you have a budget in mind?" saves everyone a round of quoting something unaffordable.

Decision date

When do they need to confirm? Vehicles cannot be held indefinitely, and this drives the validity of the quote.

Who signs

Groups usually need an agreement and a deposit. Establish who has the authority early.

Lesson 3 of 5

15.3 Building a preliminary quote

In plain words — Your job is to produce a clear, complete preliminary plan: every movement listed, every assumption stated, no committed prices unless the client's procedure lets you give them. What you hand over should be checkable at a glance.

Lay it out as a schedule

Day / timeMovementPaxVehicle
Thu 14, 10:40DFW T-D → Hyatt Regency (AA 1122, 3 pax; UA 901, 5 pax)8Sprinter
Thu 14, 14:15DFW T-A → Hyatt Regency (DL 2214)11Mini coach
Fri 15, 08:00Hyatt → Convention Center402 × mini coach
Fri 15, 17:30Convention Center → Hyatt402 × mini coach
Fri 15, 18:00–23:00VIP car, as directed2Premium sedan, 5 hrs
Sun 17, staggeredHyatt → DFW, 06:30 / 09:00 / 13:00283 × SUV + 1 coach

State the assumptions

Every group quote rests on assumptions. Writing them down is what makes the quote defensible when the event changes — and it will change.

Assumptions to state

  • Headcounts as given, subject to final numbers
  • Arrivals consolidated into waves as shown
  • Flight times as scheduled; delays may add waiting
  • Luggage: one checked bag per passenger
  • Hourly vehicles priced to the hours shown, with minimums
  • Subject to vehicle availability at time of confirmation

What to flag as open

  • Any movement where the time is not yet fixed
  • Any headcount given as "about"
  • Venue addresses not yet confirmed
  • Whether a lead vehicle or on-site coordinator is wanted
  • Parking or access restrictions at the venue
  • Overnight or split-shift driver implications
Two words that belong on every group quote you produce

"Preliminary" and "subject to availability". Until the operator has confirmed vehicles and drivers against these dates, nothing in the document is a commitment — and the customer needs to know that in writing, not by implication.

Lesson 4 of 5

15.4 When to hand it to a specialist

Groups have a handover point. Reaching it early is good work, not a failure — the damage is done by agents who press on and commit the operator to something it cannot do.

Hand over immediately when

Scale

  • More vehicles than the client's threshold (often three or more at once)
  • More than one day
  • Coaches or mini coaches of any number
  • A continuous shuttle operation

Complexity or risk

  • Multiple venues or cities
  • Anything requiring affiliates in another market
  • A named VIP, a security requirement, or a confidentiality request
  • A signed agreement, a deposit, or an RFP response
  • A date the operator is likely to be short on — a marathon, a major convention, prom season, New Year

What a good handover contains

1The movement scheduleEverything you gathered, laid out as a table. Not the email chain.
2The contactsWho enquired, who decides, who is on site, with numbers and email.
3The commercial factsBudget if given, decision date, whether they have quoted elsewhere.
4The open questionsWhat you asked and have not had back, and what you did not ask because it is above your line.
5What you have already said to the customerWord for word if you gave any indication of price or availability. The specialist must not contradict you unknowingly.
What to tell the customer while it moves

"This is a larger movement so I'm putting it with our groups team, who'll build the schedule properly — you'll hear from them by Thursday." Confident, specific, and it does not apologise for a process that exists for the customer's benefit. What you must not say is "it should be around ten thousand" on your way out the door.

Lesson 5 of 5

15.5 Knowledge check

Knowledge check

Groups and events

Pass mark: 3 of 4.

A caller asks for airport transfers for forty conference delegates. What is the correct first move?

Groups price from hours, vehicles and positioning, not from multiplied single-trip rates. Your value is a complete brief handed over early.

What is a "movement"?

Movements are the unit of work. Counting them turns a vague enquiry into something that can be planned, staffed and priced.

Which two qualifications belong on every preliminary group quote?

Until the operator has confirmed real vehicles and drivers against those dates, nothing is committed, and the customer must be told so in writing.

You have already told the customer "it'll probably be around eight thousand" before handing over. What must you do?

The customer now has a number in mind. The specialist has to know what it is before they quote, or they will contradict you unknowingly. Better still: do not give the figure at all.
Phase 7 · Light dispatch

Dispatch fundamentals

≡ Syllabus · Phase 7 · Module 16
≈ 20 min
≡Definition

Dispatch is the screen for today: every trip for the date in one table, with the driver, the car and the live status. Reservations is the order book; Dispatch is the kitchen.

»Example

09:40 — a dispatcher sees Brandon's 11:00 airport pickup still Unassigned, puts Darrell and SUV-3 on it, sets status to Dispatched, and watches it turn Assigned when Darrell accepts on his phone.

✓Key points
  • One row per trip; colour = status
  • Right-click a row for every action
  • Change status here to offer or assign drivers
  • Grid Setup lets each dispatcher shape the board
16.1 The dispatch board16.2 Set up your grid16.3 Knowledge check
